title: An affine orbit-meeting complement gives an ample boundary line
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type with geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Here a group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the group diagrams (the relative form of [def-sc-group-scheme]), and separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $X\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type, with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$ satisfying unit and associativity [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $E\subseteq X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, meaning a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Put $A=X\setminus|E|$ and suppose $A$ is affine and the restriction $H\times_SA\to X$ of $a$ is surjective on underlying points. Then the invertible module $\mathcal O_X(E)=\mathcal I_E^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-sc-invertible-module] is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No transitivity of the action on all of $X$, properness, commutativity, or Néron mapping property is assumed.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Proposition 2, printed pp.153–154 (PDF pp.159–160), applied to an effective Cartier divisor (hence an effective divisor); its relative ampleness conclusion is absolute because S is affine (Stacks Tag 01VK, morphisms.tex lemma-ample-over-affine). Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathcal O_X(E)$. The canonical-section theorem gives $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ with zero scheme $E$. Thus $X_s=A$: locally, if $\mathcal I_E=(f)$, the dual generator of $L$ identifies $s$ with $f$, so $s$ is nonzero in the residue fibre exactly off $V(f)$.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Proposition 2, printed p.153; canonical section explicitly Stacks 01X0 (divisors.tex, lemma-characterize-OD).

proof.text: Apply the invariant-component ampleness test to $L$ and the given action. It suffices to prove ampleness for every test $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ and invariant clopen connected $Y\subseteq X_T$ in that statement. Fix one and write $L_Y$ for the pullback and $s_Y$ for the pullback section. These tests provide precisely a strictly henselian trait or separably closed field, a surjective smooth $Y\to T$, and nonempty geometrically connected generic fibre; there is no connected-fibre assumption on the original $X$.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Proposition 2, printed pp.153–154, initial reductions, with generic-only components included in the cited test.

proof.text: The fibre formula for pulled-back sections gives $Y_{s_Y}=Y\cap A_T$, where $A_T=A\times_ST$. This is affine: $S,T,A$ are affine, so $A_T$ is a spectrum of a tensor-product ring; the intersection is clopen in $A_T$. Gluing the functions $1$ on that intersection and $0$ on its complement produces an idempotent $e$, and the intersection is the principal affine open $D(e)$. Base change of the given surjection yields $H_T\times_TA_T\to X_T$ surjective. Its inverse image of $Y$ equals $H_T\times_T(Y\cap A_T)$: for a point represented over a residue extension, $hu\in Y$ iff $u\in Y$, by invariance and translation by $h^{-1}$. Hence $H_T\times_TY_{s_Y}\to Y$ is surjective.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Proposition 2, affine orbit-meeting hypothesis after base change; elementary clopen-affine and inverse-action calculation expanded.

proof.text: Base change preserves smoothness and separated finite type; restriction to a clopen subscheme preserves them by restricting the same local charts and diagonal. The base-changed morphisms $m_T,i_T,e_T$ make $H_T$ a $T$-group scheme, and by invariance $a_T$ restricts to an action $H_T\times_TY\to Y$ satisfying unit and associativity. For $t\in T$ over $s\in S$, the fibre $(H_T)_t=H_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is connected, and stays connected after any extension of $\kappa(t)$, because $H_s$ is geometrically connected; so $H_T$ has geometrically connected fibres, as both cited theorems require. The square-power theorem, applied over $T$ to $H_T$ acting on $Y$, gives $r\geq1$ for which $M=L_Y^{\otimes r}$ satisfies the square condition. Smooth finite-type separated schemes over the Noetherian base $T$ have finite presentation: local finite presentation follows from the locally-Noetherian finite-type theorem, quasi-compactness from finite type and quasi-separatedness from separatedness. Thus the affine-orbit criterion applies. The section $s_Y^{\otimes r}$ of $M$ has the same nonvanishing open as $s_Y$, since a scalar in a residue field is nonzero iff its positive power is nonzero. This open is affine by the preceding step, hence lies in the union $U$ of affine positive-power section loci of $M$. Since $H_TY_{s_Y}=Y$, also $H_TU=Y$. The square-condition affine-orbit criterion proves $M$ ample.

source.place: BLR 6.3 Theorem 1 and 6.4 Proposition 2; affine-orbit assembly uses the existing Guo Corollary 6.5 criterion (March 31, 2026, printed p.16), the general square-condition version of the translation argument.

proof.text: Ampleness of $M$ implies ampleness of $L_Y$ directly from section loci: every affine open $Y_t$ supplied by a section $t$ of $M^{\otimes n}$ is the same affine open supplied by that section of $L_Y^{\otimes rn}$, and $rn\geq1$. Quasi-compactness is unchanged. We have verified all tests, so the invariant-component ampleness test gives that $L$ is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense. If $X$ is empty, its quasi-compactness and the section-locus condition are immediate.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Proposition 2, positive-power reflection and the initial local-to-global reduction; absolute ampleness uses the affine base.
